CodeHighlighter final class

Plaintext syntax highlighter for SvgRenderer / PngRenderer.

MethodSummary
__construct(public readonly string $foreground = Palettes::DRACULA['foreground'], public readonly string $keyword = Palettes::DRACULA['pink'], public readonly string $string = Palettes::DRACULA['yellow'], public readonly string $number = Palettes::DRACULA['purple'], public readonly string $comment = Palettes::DRACULA['comment'])
static forTheme(Theme $theme): selfBuild a highlighter whose TokenKind::Plain colour tracks the given theme's foreground. Syntax accents come from the theme's own token slots when it carries them (imported VS Code / flat-palette themes repaint CODE from their tokenColors); slots that are null fall back to accents that stay readable on the theme's background: the Dracula set on dark themes, a GitHub-Light-ish set on pale ones.

flush(): voidPush buffered bytes to disk. Unlike write(), flush() on an already closed writer stays a silent no-op instead of raising — the asymmetry is deliberate and narrower than it looks.

Lang final class

Per-library translation facade for candy-codeshot.

MethodSummary
static t(string $key, array $params = []): stringInterpolated parameters are attacker-controlled text: flags, paths and format names come from argv, and argv can carry raw ESC/CSI bytes. Every Lang::t() message here lands on STDERR in front of a terminal, so a forged OSC-8 hyperlink or CSI rebind would otherwise execute verbatim. Sweeping each parameter through Sanitize::untrustedForDisplay() at this single choke is cheaper than policing every call site — the catalogs themselves stay authored (trusted) text.

Theme final class

Visual theme shared by SvgRenderer and PngRenderer. Carries the colours of every surface the renderers paint (background, foreground, frame chrome, window controls, line highlight band), plus typographic settings (font family, size, line height). The active window-chrome style lives on the renderers, not the theme.
